en: Anna, how much is one kilo of tomatoes today?
tamil: அண்ணா, இன்னைக்கு ஒரு கிலோ தக்காளி என்ன விலை?
context: Asking a vegetable seller the price.
explain: 'How much' is used to ask the price of something. 'Today' shows prices can change daily.
usage: Use it at a vegetable market before you buy anything.
leelaQ: How much do you pay for tomatoes these days?
answer: I usually pay around thirty rupees for a kilo of tomatoes.

en: I will take two kilos if you reduce the rate.
tamil: நீங்க ரேட்டை குறைச்சா ரெண்டு கிலோ வாங்கிக்கிறேன்.
context: Offering to buy more for a lower price.
explain: 'If you reduce the rate' is the condition. 'I will take' is the result you promise.
usage: Use it while bargaining with a shopkeeper when you want to buy more.
leelaQ: What do you say when you want a better price in a market?
answer: I say that I will buy more if the shopkeeper reduces the price.

en: Please don't give me a plastic bag, I have my own cloth bag.
tamil: ப்ளாஸ்டிக் பை வேண்டாம், என்கிட்ட துணிப்பை இருக்கு.
context: Refusing a plastic bag at a shop.
explain: 'Don't give me' is a polite negative command. The reason follows after the comma.
usage: Use it at the billing counter when you carry your own bag.
leelaQ: Do you carry a cloth bag when you go shopping?
answer: Yes, I always keep a cloth bag in my scooter.

en: Is this mango sweet or sour?
tamil: இந்த மாம்பழம் இனிப்பா, புளிப்பா?
context: Checking the taste before buying fruit.
explain: 'Sweet or sour?' gives two choices, so the seller can answer in one word.
usage: Use it at a fruit stall before you buy mangoes.
leelaQ: Which fruit do you like the most?
answer: I like mangoes the most because they are very sweet.

en: Can you weigh it once again, please?
tamil: இன்னொரு தடவை எடை போட்டு காட்டுங்க, please.
context: Asking a seller to check the weight.
explain: 'Can you' with 'please' is a polite request. 'Once again' means one more time.
usage: Use it when you think the weight on the scale is not correct.
leelaQ: What will you do if the weight looks wrong?
answer: I will politely ask the seller to weigh it once again.

en: The vegetables here are always fresh in the morning.
tamil: இங்க காலையில காய்கறி எப்பவும் ஃப்ரெஷ்ஷா இருக்கும்.
context: Telling a friend why you shop early.
explain: 'Always' with the simple present talks about a habit or a regular fact.
usage: Use it when you recommend a market or shop to a friend.
leelaQ: When do you go to the market, morning or evening?
answer: I go in the morning because the vegetables are fresh.

en: I bought these bananas for forty rupees a dozen.
tamil: இந்த வாழைப்பழத்தை டஜன் நாற்பது ரூபாய்க்கு வாங்கினேன்.
context: Telling someone what you paid.
explain: 'Bought' is the past of 'buy'. 'A dozen' means twelve pieces.
usage: Use it when family or neighbours ask how much you paid.
leelaQ: What did you buy at the market last time?
answer: I bought some bananas and a few onions last time.

en: Give me a quarter kilo of green chillies.
tamil: கால் கிலோ பச்சை மிளகாய் கொடுங்க.
context: Ordering a small quantity at a stall.
explain: 'Quarter kilo' means 250 grams. Add 'please' to sound more polite.
usage: Use it at a vegetable shop when you need only a small amount.
leelaQ: How much chilli do you use for cooking at home?
answer: We use only a quarter kilo of chillies in a week.

en: You are charging me more because I am new here.
tamil: நான் புதுசுன்னு என்கிட்ட அதிகமா வாங்குறீங்க.
context: Complaining politely about a higher price.
explain: 'You are charging' describes what is happening now. 'Because' gives the reason.
usage: Use it when you feel a seller is asking a tourist price.
leelaQ: Have you ever paid more than the real price?
answer: Yes, once a shopkeeper charged me double at a temple market.

en: That shop is cheaper, so I am going there.
tamil: அந்த கடையில விலை குறைவு, அதனால அங்க போறேன்.
context: Walking away to a cheaper shop.
explain: 'So' joins the reason and the result. 'Am going' shows a plan happening now.
usage: Use it as a polite way to leave when the price is too high.
leelaQ: Do you compare prices before buying something?
answer: Yes, I check two or three shops before I buy.

en: Have you got change for a five hundred rupee note?
tamil: ஐநூறு ரூபாய் நோட்டுக்கு சில்லறை இருக்கா?
context: Asking a shopkeeper for change.
explain: 'Have you got' is a common way to ask if someone has something. 'Change' means small notes or coins.
usage: Use it at small shops when you only have a big note.
leelaQ: What do you do when a shop has no change?
answer: I pay by UPI or buy something small to get change.

en: We have been shopping in this market for ten years.
tamil: நாங்க இந்த மார்க்கெட்டுல பத்து வருஷமா வாங்குறோம்.
context: Telling a seller you are a regular customer.
explain: 'Have been shopping' with 'for ten years' shows an action that started in the past and continues.
usage: Use it to ask a regular seller for a better price.
leelaQ: Where does your family usually shop for groceries?
answer: We usually shop at the market near our house.

en: I never buy fruits from the roadside without checking them.
tamil: நான் ரோட்டோரத்துல பழம் பார்க்காம வாங்கவே மாட்டேன்.
context: Explaining your careful shopping habit.
explain: 'Never' makes the sentence negative. 'Without checking' means before checking.
usage: Use it when you talk about being careful with food and money.
leelaQ: How do you check fruits before buying?
answer: I press them gently and smell them before buying.

en: Keep the change, thank you.
tamil: மீதி சில்லறை வெச்சுக்கோங்க, நன்றி.
context: Telling a helper to keep the extra money.
explain: 'Keep the change' means you do not want the extra money back. It is polite with 'thank you'.
usage: Use it with an auto driver or a helper when you want to tip.
leelaQ: When do you give a small tip to someone?
answer: I give a small tip when someone helps me carry heavy bags.

en: The jasmine flowers smell so good today!
tamil: இன்னைக்கு மல்லிப்பூ ரொம்ப வாசனையா இருக்கு!
context: Enjoying the flowers at a flower stall.
explain: 'Smell good' describes the nice smell. 'So' makes the feeling stronger.
usage: Use it at a flower stall, or when someone brings flowers home.
leelaQ: Do you buy flowers for your house?
answer: Yes, I buy jasmine flowers every Friday for the pooja.

en: Could you show me the other colour as well?
tamil: மத்த கலரையும் காட்டுவீங்களா?
context: Asking a seller to show more options.
explain: 'Could you' is softer and more polite than 'Can you'. 'As well' means also.
usage: Use it in a cloth shop when you want to compare colours.
leelaQ: What colour do you like for your clothes?
answer: I like blue and green colours for my shirts.

en: He will bargain until the price comes down.
tamil: விலை குறையுற வரைக்கும் அவன் பேரம் பேசுவான்.
context: Describing a friend who bargains a lot.
explain: 'Until' shows the point where the action stops. 'Will' shows what he is going to do.
usage: Use it when you describe someone who likes to bargain.
leelaQ: Are you good at bargaining?
answer: Not really, but I try to ask for a small discount.

en: I can't pay more than three hundred.
tamil: முன்னூறுக்கு மேல என்னால கொடுக்க முடியாது.
context: Stating your maximum price.
explain: 'Can't pay more than' sets a limit. It is a firm but polite way to bargain.
usage: Use it when you want to end bargaining at your budget.
leelaQ: What do you say when something is above your budget?
answer: I say that it is too costly and I cannot pay that much.

en: Where can I find fresh coriander leaves?
tamil: புது கொத்தமல்லி தழை எங்க கிடைக்கும்?
context: Asking where to find an item in the market.
explain: 'Where can I find' is a useful way to ask for the location of a thing.
usage: Use it when the item you need is not at the stall in front of you.
leelaQ: What do you do when you cannot find something in a shop?
answer: I ask the shopkeeper where I can find it.

en: My mother always buys vegetables from the same seller.
tamil: எங்கம்மா எப்பவும் ஒரே கடைக்காரர்கிட்டதான் காய்கறி வாங்குவாங்க.
context: Talking about a family habit.
explain: 'Always' and 'buys' show a regular habit. 'The same' means not a different one.
usage: Use it when you talk about your family shopping habits.
leelaQ: Who does the shopping at your home?
answer: My mother does most of the shopping at home.

en: Please pack these separately.
tamil: இதெல்லாம் தனித்தனியா பேக் பண்ணுங்க.
context: Asking a seller to pack things apart.
explain: 'Separately' means not together. 'Please' makes the order polite.
usage: Use it when you buy items that should not touch each other, like fish and fruit.
leelaQ: How do you pack things when you carry them home?
answer: I put the heavy things at the bottom of the bag.

en: I picked the best tomatoes myself.
tamil: நல்ல தக்காளியை நானே பார்த்து எடுத்தேன்.
context: Proudly telling your family about your choice.
explain: 'Picked' is the past of 'pick'. 'Myself' stresses that you did it, not someone else.
usage: Use it when you come home from the market and tell your family.
leelaQ: Do you like choosing vegetables yourself?
answer: Yes, I like choosing them myself so they are good.

en: Are these sarees handloom or machine made?
tamil: இந்த புடவைங்க கைத்தறியா, மெஷின்ல செஞ்சதா?
context: Asking a shopkeeper about the cloth.
explain: 'Handloom or machine made' gives two choices. 'Are these' is used for many things.
usage: Use it in a cloth shop when you care about quality and price.
leelaQ: What do you check before buying a saree or shirt?
answer: I check the cloth quality and the colour carefully.

en: I will come back after looking at two more shops.
tamil: இன்னும் ரெண்டு கடை பார்த்துட்டு திரும்ப வர்றேன்.
context: Politely leaving without buying.
explain: 'After looking at' is used with -ing. It is a polite way to leave a shop.
usage: Use it when you are not ready to buy now but may buy later.
leelaQ: What do you say when you do not want to buy something?
answer: I say thank you and tell them I will come back later.

en: Is this the final price or can we talk a little more?
tamil: இதுதான் கடைசி விலையா, இல்ல இன்னும் கொஞ்சம் பேசலாமா?
context: Checking if the seller can reduce more.
explain: 'Or' joins two choices. 'A little more' is a soft way to ask for more discount.
usage: Use it at the end of bargaining to see if there is room for a small discount.
leelaQ: How do you feel about bargaining at a market?
answer: I enjoy it because I can save a little money.
